title: Introduce microstrip-attn pipeline with asymmetric-tile prefetch and fused-rope optimizer
author: Ava Morgan
description:
Motivation: We observed that real-world request lengths and prompt distributions at scale are highly asymmetric (many short queries interleaved with occasional long contexts). Existing tiled attention kernels assume symmetric tiling or fall back to a slower generic path when shapes are irregular, which hurts p99 latency and throughput for mixed workloads. This PR introduces a new microstrip attention pipeline that supports asymmetric tile sizes, combined with a fused rope/rotary optimizer to reduce operator overhead and memory traffic. The patch also adds scheduler hints for continuous batching and a KV cache eviction heuristic that prefers compacting hot prefixes ahead of eviction to reduce cache misses.

What changed (high-level):
- New kernel: runtime/attn/microstrip_kernel.cu implements the microstrip attention path. It tiles Q/K/V in variable-width microstrips, enabling efficient vector loads for short and medium sequences without paying the cost for full-tile padding.
- Fused rope/rotary: runtime/attn/fused_rope.cpp and fused_rope.cu implement a single fused CUDA kernel that applies rotary embedding, rope remapping for legacy models that use 'rope swap' patterns, and a precision-aware accumulation stage to maintain fp16 stability at long sequences.
- Prefetch scheduler: runtime/scheduler/continuous_batcher.cc adds a prefetch hint generator that informs the microstrip kernel about likely next-prefix lengths to reduce KV cache latency on continuous streams. The scheduler integrates with existing autoscaling hints and has a config knob to opt in per-model.
- KV eviction heuristic: runtime/kv_cache/evict_policy.cc updates the eviction logic to attempt hot-prefix compaction before evicting whole shards; adds metrics (kv.evictions.compactions, kv.evictions.fallbacks).
- API/test/benchmarks: benches/bench_microstrip.py and tests/attn_microstrip_test.cpp with deterministic microbench harness for typical Redwood workloads. Performance regression guard added to CI.

Compatibility and fallbacks:
- The microstrip path is guarded behind device capability checks and a runtime flag (ATTN_MICROSTRIP_ENABLED). On unsupported devices we automatically route to the existing tiled path. A runtime assertion ensures behavioral parity for short sequences in debug builds.

Benchmarks (summary):
- Mixed short/long workload (80% <= 128 tokens, 20% up to 2k tokens) on A100-40GB: throughput +28% for generation throughput (tokens/sec) at median latency, p99 latency down by 14% compared to mainline fused-flash kernel; cost-per-token reduction ~9% due to fewer wasted loads and better KV locality.
- Long-only workloads (>1k tokens): parity with existing fused-flash kernel (within 2%).

Checklist:
- [x] Kernel correctness tests (unit + randomized)
- [x] Numerical stability tests (accumulation checks vs baseline)
- [x] Benchmarks and perf dashboards updated
- [x] CI regression guard
- [x] Documentation comment blocks in critical files

References: Linear ENG-1482 (microstrip kernel), ENG-1620 (continuous batching hints). Related PRs: earlier rope/rotary fusion efforts (see PRs in the repo history) but this is a distinct microstrip design and introduces the KV compaction heuristic.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the memory model in microstrip_kernel.cu (comments explain data layout) and the interaction between the scheduler hints and eviction policy. I left the tuning constants (MICROSTRIP_MIN_WIDTH, PREFETCH_LOOKAHEAD) as config flags in runtime/config/attn_flags.h for easier experimentation.

Migration notes: default behavior unchanged. Operators who want to enable the new path can set the runtime flag or allow the autotuner to enable it when device caps match.

Risks: the most likely risk is subtle differences in fp16 accumulation for extremely long sequences; extensive tests were added and a debug parity check is enabled in dev builds.

release_notes:
- Added microstrip attention kernel for asymmetric tiling and improved mixed-workload throughput
- Fused rope/rotary kernel to reduce operator overhead and improve fp16 stability
- Scheduler prefetch hints for continuous batching and KV cache compaction heuristic
- No behavioral breaking changes; feature is opt-in via ATTN_MICROSTRIP_ENABLED
